subject: Commitment tier qualification and legal lead-time
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@orion-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:03:00Z
Subject: Commitment tier qualification and legal lead-time

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and the asks we put on our side so procurement/legal have clear timing: 

Summary from the call
- Target workload: interactive recommendation scoring + feature generation for search. Avg sequence length ~150 tokens, peak concurrent sessions around 60 QPS across EU/US.
- Expected steady-state token volume: 5–10M tokens / month (likely ramp to high end over 2 quarters).
- Business target for unit economics: looking for a target between $1,800–$3,000 per 1M tokens depending on commitment/SLAs.
- Current procurement behavior: vendor onboarding + PO required for monthly spend > $20k, and legal needs a standard SaaS addendum for any annual spend > $200k.

What we (Redwood) will provide by end of day tomorrow:
- A concise pricing one-pager with mapped commitment tiers and monthly spend bands (attached).
- A draft SOW template and proposed billing cadence (attached: SOW_orion_draft.docx).
- A suggested mutual action plan (MAP) with target legal lead-time and milestones.

Questions / asks for you
1) Can you confirm whether procurement requires a PO for any multi-month pilot, or only once monthly invoicing exceeds $20k?
2) Do you have a preferred legal approver and an expected review window (typical windows we see are 2–3 weeks for an NDA/SaaS addendum, 4–6 weeks if there are custom terms)?
3) If we were to propose a 6-month committed tier, what minimum monthly commit would make procurement easier on your side (i.e., a threshold that avoids extra procurement gates)?

Next steps
- I’ll send the pricing anchors and MAP now; if the numbers look close we can ask your procurement contact for the PO routing template so we can draft payment terms that match their system.

[Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: SOW_orion_draft.docx]

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@orion-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Barker <tbarker@orion-retail.com>, procurement@orion-retail.com
Date: 2026-10-11T18:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Commitment tier qualification and legal lead-time

Thanks Logan — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PO requirement: Procurement confirmed verbally that any recurring monthly spend over $20k requires a PO. For pilots under 3 months we can sometimes route through a credit card or one-off invoice, but that needs approvals.
- Legal: Our legal lead is Tom Barker (cc’d). Typical review for standard SaaS terms + SOW is ~3 weeks; if there are custom IP/data terms it can go longer.
- Procurement gate: to avoid an extended procurement process we’d ideally keep monthly commit below $18k during the initial 3-month pilot. After pilot, moving to a 6–12 month commit would be evaluated by Finance.

Requests:
1) Please send the pricing one-pager with explicit monthly cost examples (show 3 scenarios: 3M, 7M, 12M tokens/mo) and what the effective $/1M token is at each commit level.
2) Any security or SOC2 docs we should expect to attach to our vendor onboarding?

If you can get those in the next 24–36 hours that would help us queue the procurement ticket.

—Elena
Director, Data Products | Orion Retail
elena@orion-retail.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@orion-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Barker <tbarker@orion-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Commitment tier qualification and legal lead-time

Elena / Tom — thanks for the quick clarifications. Attaching the one-pager you requested and summarizing three concrete pricing scenarios so procurement can map to PO thresholds: 

Pricing anchors (examples) — effective cost per 1M tokens shown per tier
- Scenario A (short pilot, PAYG): 3M tokens/mo -> PAYG rate $3,200 / 1M -> monthly $9,600
- Scenario B (6-month modest commit): 7M tokens/mo -> committed rate $2,400 / 1M -> monthly $16,800
- Scenario C (12-month annual commit): 12M tokens/mo -> committed rate $2,000 / 1M -> monthly $24,000

Notes on procurement mapping
- Scenario A keeps monthly spend < $20k and should be routable without a formal PO (card or single-invoice option for pilot).
- Scenario B sits around $16.8k/mo and matches your suggested <$18k pilot threshold — procurement should be able to approve faster.
- Scenario C is >$20k/mo so will require a PO and likely the standard vendor onboarding. If you want to avoid the PO, we can structure a ramping commit that keeps the first 2–3 months under the $20k gate and then transitions.

Security and onboarding docs
- We’ll share a SOC2 snapshot, vendor security questionnaire answers, and our standard DPA. I’ve linked the doc folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPricingOnePager

Proposed MAP / timing
- Day 0 (today): Share pricing one-pager + SOW draft (attached).
- Day 1–3: Client reviews pricing and confirms preferred scenario (A/B/C).
- Day 3–10: Legal review of SOW/terms (target 1–2 weeks for standard terms).
- Day 7–21: Procurement issues PO (if required) and vendor onboarding finishes; billing starts on agreed start date.

If this looks correct I’ll: (1) open an internal deal record RDW-4851, (2) route a short credit option for the first invoice if procurement timing is >2 weeks, and (3) request Marissa to prepare the SOW with the chosen scenario filled in.

[Attachment: redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf]

Best — Logan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Commitment tier qualification and legal lead-time

Quick internal note — I recommend we offer a one-month credit to bridge Orion’s procurement lead-time if they pick Scenario C but need 2–3 weeks for PO. That keeps momentum without changing the anchor pricing.

Action items for us:
- Marissa: please draft the SOW for Scenario B and C so we can flip quickly.
- Logan: confirm whether offering a short credit needs approvals (I think 1 month credit < $25k is OK under regional promotions).

I’ll also add the RDW-4851 tag and a short internal note on expected ARR if they convert to Scenario C.

—Ben
